long_description:
500 Days in the Wild | Q&A Screening
Director and Star Dianna Whelan joins Penthouse Cinema for an exclusive screening of 500 Days in the Wild, following with a Q&A session after the film.

500 Days In The Wild follows the epic 6-year journey of filmmaker Dianne Whelan as she sets out to reconnect with nature and become the first person to travel the world’s longest trail.

The 24,000 km Trans Canada Trail stretches across the continent of North America, connecting the Atlantic, Arctic and Pacific oceans. It is the longest trail in the world. For six years filmmaker Dianne Whelan traveled the entirety of the land and water trails, the only person to ever accomplish this journey. 500 Days in the Wild recounts Dianne’s journey by bike, canoe, skis, snowshoes and on foot and her cross-cultural visits with those who live close to the land.

This feature doc culled from 800 hours of footage is an intricate weave of adventure film, personal reflection and stunning captures of wildlife and landscapes. Using humour, adventure, beautiful cinematography and a great soundtrack (including songs from Joni Mitchell, First Aid Kit, Xavier Rudd, and The Tragically Hip), 500 Days in the Wild will entertain audiences and inspire hope for the future.

She started out alone, disillusioned with state of the world, to look for different ways of caring for the land and for each other. She ended the journey a bit wiser, more hopeful, in love and with a passion to share this story.

Winner - Grand Prize VIMFF
Winner - Best Film World Trail Film Festival
Winner - Best Film Nordic Adventure Film Festival
Winner - Audience Award - Victoria Film Festival

Join PopRox favs Austin and Tara for a 6 week introduction to character and narrative. Improv is so much more than games, and this is the course that starts to branch into storytelling and narrative.

A perfect next step for those who've done an intro course this year, want to give narrative improv a go, or are looking for a refresher on the basics of character and narrative.

About this Event



*********

Don’t look down. The sky is clear and blue. When you breathe in for the first time after your months-long voyage, the fresh air tastes impossibly sweet.

Don’t look down. A single star rests in the heavens, yellow and warm. Shoals of silvery fish dart through picturesque waves.

Don’t look down. The islands quake and churn beneath your feet. Alerts appear hourly on your screens about impossibilities, measurements beyond rational explanation.

You look down. What lies beneath? What might be unearthed from the strata of the past? What has been forgotten? And what should have remained buried?




What's going on?

A week ago, three ships landed on the planet called Etsen. The Highmit Research Mission has journeyed to this planet, across the vast dangers of space, to help the planet’s scientists understand the impossibility of measuring a second star in a 100 kilometre diameter patch of their sky.

You landed at Scion. It’s small, compared to the average communities on your home planets. Not even 5000 people. But it’s the largest settlement in Etsen’s affected zone. And it’s a strange new environment for many of you, perched on an island in a temperate archipelago.

The research mission’s primary team has already set up their main base of operations in Scion. Alongside the limited number of specialised Etsenite scientists, they are beginning initial research into the planet’s anomaly.

A few days ago, a small settlement in the affected zone, Axis, reported abnormal technological errors. Yesterday, a different settlement, closer to Scion, reported similar malfunctions.

You are members of the secondary research team dispatched to Axis. Your task sounds simple enough.

Identify the cause of the errors.
Prevent them from spreading further.

But, just like the impossible second star, you suspect nothing is as simple as it seems.

WELL AHEAD: PUT YOUR HEALTH ON THE AGENDA


An event for women balancing demanding careers, businesses and families, who are already invested in their health and want to understand it more deeply.

As energy, sleep, recovery and body composition shift through midlife, the right information matters.


Well Ahead brings together Dame Susan Devoy and a lineup of experts across health, nutrition, movement and healthy ageing to explore the science and strategy behind:


* Energy and recovery

* Sleep and stress

* Nutrition

* Strength and movement

* Body composition

* Hormonal changes

* Perimenopause and menopause

* Bone health

* Genetics and individual biology



Well Ahead is designed as a connected conversation, not a series of standalone talks.


Each speaker builds on the last, giving you a clearer, more complete picture of your own health rather than a list of disconnected tips.


The day opens with an optional workshop, Your Genes, Your Choices, exploring genetics, DNA testing and the role our genes can play in understanding individual biology. The full programme continues into the afternoon and closes with a live panel and audience Q&A.


Practical information. Expert perspectives. One day, properly invested in your health.


Choose a Morning Workshop pass, Main Event pass, or the Full Pass for the whole day.

----------------------------------------


> > “Women spend so much of their lives looking after everyone and everything else. Well Ahead is about putting your own health on the agenda, hearing from people who really know their field, and coming away with information and ideas you can actually use. You don't have to have all the answers. Sometimes you just need to make the time to start asking the right questions.”

- Dame Susan Devoy



Well Ahead is supported by a growing network of organisations across Wellington's business, professional, health, fitness and wellness communities, all helping us bring women together for an important conversation about health through midlife.

----------------------------------------


ABOUT CONQUER HEALTH

Conquer Health helps men and women understand their unique biology, so they can focus on what matters to their health today and make informed choices for the years ahead. Rather than one-size-fits-all health advice, Conquer Health combines advanced biological testing with a multidisciplinary clinical team to build a personalised picture of your health, delivered remotely anywhere in New Zealand.

Men’s Circle: Rooted in Connection

The evening offers a supportive space for men to come together, connect, and speak openly about life. Whether you’re moving through a period of change, looking for deeper connection, or simply wanting a space where you can show up as you are, you’re welcome here.

The conversations are honest, open, and grounded in mutual respect. There’s no pressure to speak, share, or have everything figured out. You’re just as welcome to listen and be present. Together, we create a space rooted in confidentiality and non-judgement, where everyone can feel safe, heard, and free to be themselves.


Structure of the Circle
Gathering in a Circle: Participants sit in a circle to symbolize equality and unity.
A short meditation or moment of silence may be included to help everyone arrive and connect.
Talking Object: A sharing stick or object is placed in the center. Only the person holding the object may speak, ensuring uninterrupted sharing.
Open Sharing: Anyone may choose to share while holding the object. Sharing is optional, and passing is always respected.
Active Listening: While one person shares, others listen attentively without speaking, interrupting, or offering advice. The focus is on witnessing and being present.
No Judgments or Advice: Participants refrain from judging or offering unsolicited advice, creating a safe space for authentic expression.
Closing: The circle may conclude with a group reflection, a moment of gratitude, or a simple acknowledgment of the shared experience.

Circle Agreements
Supportive Environment: We are here to uplift and support one another, fostering trust and brotherhood.
Focus on the Present: Share what's alive for you now, focusing on your emotions and experiences to deepen emotional awareness.
Use "I" Statements: Speak from your personal perspective using "I" statements to promote authenticity and responsibility. Avoid generalizations like "we" or "us."
No Judgment or fixing: Refrain from judging others sharing or offering unsolicited advice, ensuring a safe and non-critical space.
Confidentiality: What is shared in the circle stays in the circle. You may discuss your own experience outside the group but keep others' details private.








After the circle, stay for a wholesome plant-based dinner and dessert ($20 or $10 for students). Sharing a meal is a simple way to extend the sense of community and connection. This gathering is offered on a non-profit basis.


Meet Your Host: Sri Jiva

Since childhood, Sri Jiva has been fascinated by meaning, purpose, and authentic life fulfilment. This, among other things, led him to join a monastery at the age of 19. After years of monastic training, he chose to marry and pursue a career. He felt called to use his monastic experience to help others understand themselves, and to find wisdom, meaning, and purpose in their own lives. Inspired by this calling, he went to university to study counselling. It’s in the Ballot” is a community-led awareness and participation initiative. We aim to increase voter interest in the general and council elections nationally.

By using broadcasting and web-based technologies to deliver in-studio; online on Facebook, YouTube and Twitch; and edited as YouTube videos we aim to enable voters to make informed voting decisions.

About this Event


Guided Kundalini Activation





Events now start at 6pm. Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.



A guided kundalini activation. Breath of fire and kundalini pranayama, simple repetitive movement, sound and stillness, sequenced to wake up energy that has been sitting dormant along the spine and let it move.


Who is this for

People who already have some breathwork or movement practice and want something more activating than a wind-down class. You are curious about kundalini but want it held by someone who works with the nervous system, not bypasses it. You are willing to feel a lot and stop when you need to.

Not the right fit as a first-ever breathwork experience. The Root or a gentler breath class is a better start.


What to expect
Arrival and a short orientation: what kundalini activation is, what is normal, and how to opt out of anything
Progressive breath and movement rounds that build energy and heat
A peak where the practice is most active: emotion, shaking, heat, tingling, sound can all come up, all normal
A long, quiet integration: stillness, slow breath, nothing to do
A few minutes to land and share if you want to, before you leave

Benefits
A felt sense of energy moving where it had been stuck
Emotional release without needing a story for it
A reset for a system that has been running flat or wired-and-tired
A clearer, more spacious baseline for a day or two afterward

(No health claims. This is a practice, not a treatment.)


Pre-class prep
Skip heavy food and alcohol in the hours before.
Eat something light beforehand, not a full meal.
Come a few minutes early to settle
If you are pregnant, have a heart or blood-pressure condition, epilepsy, glaucoma, recent surgery, or are in acute mental-health crisis, message Lynn before booking so she can advise or adapt
Wear layers you can move in and get warm in.

Contraindications

Kundalini pranayama and breath of fire are intense. Please do not book, or check with Lynn first, if any of these apply: pregnancy, cardiovascular disease or uncontrolled high blood pressure, epilepsy or seizure history, glaucoma or detached retina, recent abdominal or chest surgery, acute psychosis or an unstable mental-health condition. If you feel dizzy or overwhelmed at any point you stop, breathe normally, and rest, that is always allowed.

Lynn’s work blends three pillars:

Somatic breathwork to regulate the nervous system, soften protective patterns, and restore a steadier baseline in the body
Reiki to support energetic clearing, heart coherence, deep rest, and integration, in a gentle, consent-based way
Life coaching to translate what opens in a session into grounded change in relationships, work, boundaries, and daily life

Lynn’s approach is trauma-aware, practical, and spiritually spacious. The focus isn’t on forcing transformation, it’s on creating enough safety for your system to unwind, receive support, and reconnect with its natural capacity for calm, clarity, and connection.

Join Catherine Robertson and a panel of writers as they find words for the books that have found them speechless.
